skill.name: develop-userscripts
skill.description: Develop browser userscripts for Tampermonkey and ScriptCat, including metadata blocks, GM APIs, permissions, UserConfig, background scripts, cron scripts, and subscription packages.
skill.summary: Build, debug, package, and publish Tampermonkey or ScriptCat userscripts with correct metadata and permissions.
skill.author: xixu-me

security_audit.summary: Static analysis primarily flagged Markdown examples, documentation URLs, inline code markers, and userscript permission terms. I found no evidence of prompt injection, command execution, credential theft, or filesystem access in the reviewed files. The skill is dual-use because it teaches userscript networking and subscriptions, so generated scripts still need normal security review.

content.user_title: Develop Userscripts for Tampermonkey and ScriptCat
content.value_statement: Userscripts often fail because metadata, permissions, and runtime behavior do not match. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through portable Tampermonkey and ScriptCat development.
actual_capabilities: Builds metadata blocks with @match, @grant, @connect, @run-at, and update URLs.
Chooses between portable foreground scripts, ScriptCat background scripts, cron scripts, and subscription bundles.
Explains GM storage, requests, notifications, clipboard, resources, menu commands, and tab APIs.
Troubleshoots permission, injection timing, CSP, Manifest V3, and manager behavior issues.
Guides UserConfig, UserSubscribe, CloudCat caveats, publishing metadata, and update behavior.
limitations: Does not replace current Tampermonkey or ScriptCat documentation for every API version.
Does not audit generated userscripts for legal, privacy, or site terms compliance.
Does not cover full browser extension architecture outside userscript managers.
Needs target sites, permissions, and runtime requirements to produce safe metadata.

use_cases.title: Build a page enhancement script
use_cases.description: Create a portable Tampermonkey script with scoped matches, required grants, and predictable injection timing.

use_cases.title: Debug ScriptCat background work
use_cases.description: Resolve async completion, logging, retry, and Manifest V3 issues in ScriptCat background or cron scripts.

use_cases.title: Package a userscript release
use_cases.description: Prepare update metadata, subscription bundles, UserConfig settings, and publishing checks before sharing scripts.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic userscript
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a portable page script.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Tampermonkey userscript for [site] that [goal]. Use the smallest safe @match, @grant, and @connect set.

prompt_templates.title: Fix runtime permissions
prompt_templates.scenario: Debug a script that installs but does not behave correctly.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my userscript behavior: [symptoms]. Check metadata, injection timing, GM API grants, @connect hosts, and manager logs.

prompt_templates.title: Design ScriptCat automation
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for background or scheduled work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a ScriptCat [background or cron] script for [task]. Include async completion, retry behavior, logging, and runtime limitations.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a subscription release
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my ScriptCat subscription plan for [scripts]. Check update metadata, HTTPS links, permissions, UserConfig, and user consent risks.

output_examples.input: I need a Tampermonkey script that highlights overdue rows and checks a status API.
output_examples.output: The response proposes a scoped metadata block, the needed GM APIs, an explicit connect host, and a safe document-idle runtime plan.

output_examples.input: My ScriptCat cron script starts a request but exits before the request finishes.
output_examples.output: The response explains promise completion, retry handling, run logs, and how to keep work inside the scheduled interval.

output_examples.input: I want to publish two related scripts as a ScriptCat subscription.
output_examples.output: The response outlines subscription metadata, HTTPS installation links, permission review, versioning, and update behavior for users.

best_practices: Declare only the matching hosts and GM APIs needed for the script.
Test foreground and background behavior in the actual userscript manager runtime.
Keep update URLs, versions, and subscription permissions clear before publishing.
anti_patterns: Using wildcard @connect or broad @match rules when specific hosts work.
Mixing Tampermonkey foreground patterns with ScriptCat background-only behavior.
Publishing subscription updates without clear permission review and user consent.

faq.question: Which userscript managers does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on Tampermonkey and ScriptCat, including portable patterns and ScriptCat-only features.

faq.question: Can it help with ScriptCat background and cron scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers runtime choice, async completion, logging, retry behavior, and cron interval concerns.

faq.question: Does it build full browser extensions?
faq.answer: No. It is for userscript managers, not complete extension architecture or Web Store packaging.

faq.question: How does it handle network permissions?
faq.answer: It asks for explicit @connect hosts and explains when GM_xmlhttpRequest is required.

faq.question: Can it debug CSP and injection timing issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare page scripts, background scripts, @run-at values, manager logs, and browser settings.

faq.question: Is it safe for API tokens?
faq.answer: It recommends avoiding hardcoded secrets and reviewing storage behavior before publishing any script.
